title: ImageNet-trained CNNs are not biased towards texture: Revisiting feature re

predicted_errors.supporting_evidence: The allocation described is arithmetically impossible as written. The paper states that each participant saw only one version of each image, that the five conditions were 'split across groups of five participants,' and that only 20 participants completed the study. If every image version is to be evaluated by five participants, this requires 5 conditions × 5 participants = 25 observations per image, hence at least 25 participants when each participant sees one version of each image. With 20 participants there can be only four observations per image on average. The claim of balanced five-participant coverage must be corrected or the actual allocation reported.

The text first says that model predictions 'were determined using the argmax class across all subclasses without thresholding.' It immediately then says that 'complementary results using argmax to define class predictions are reported in the supplemental material.' These cannot describe two distinct procedures: the main procedure is already explicitly argmax. Either the main evaluation used a different aggregation/thresholding procedure or the supplemental comparison is mislabeled.

The method claims to validate suppression effects for each of the three feature types, including color: 'we validate the suppression effects of these transformations using quantitative metrics.' However, Table 2 contains only texture and shape quantities (LV, HFE, Edge-SSIM, and gradient correlation). It supplies no metric at all for preservation or suppression of chromatic information, despite grayscale and channel shuffle being central proposed transformations. Thus the stated quantitative validation does not validate one-third of the framework.

The conclusion that CNNs rely more on local shape than texture is not supported by the reported suppression comparison because the two manipulations demonstrably remove very unequal amounts of their nominal targets and also damage different non-target information. In Table 2, the selected grid-6 patch shuffle reduces the reported shape score to 0.176 while leaving the reported texture score at 1.000, whereas bilateral filtering leaves a texture score of 0.521 and also leaves shape at 0.796. A much larger accuracy loss under patch shuffle than bilateral filtering therefore does not establish greater shape reliance; it can result from substantially stronger information destruction and transformation artifacts. The paper itself acknowledges incomplete isolation, yet still presents the result as evidence against the ImageNet texture-bias claim.

predicted_errors.error_location: Section 5.2, Medical Imaging discussion versus Figure 4d–f
predicted_errors.supporting_evidence: Figure 4d–f is described as containing BloodMNIST, BreastMNIST, DermaMNIST, OCTMNIST, and PathMNIST. The corresponding text instead discusses effects in RetinaMNIST and DermaMNIST and identifies ChestMNIST as the sole grayscale exception. RetinaMNIST and ChestMNIST are not among the five datasets shown in the figure. Consequently, the narrative does not describe the plotted experiment and the stated set of datasets must be reconciled.

The claim that grayscale/color suppression substantially reduces accuracy for most of the Figure 4 medical datasets 'except in ChestMNIST, which contains only grayscale images' is factually incompatible with the displayed dataset list. BreastMNIST and OCTMNIST in Figure 4 are also grayscale MedMNIST datasets, so grayscale conversion should be an identity operation on their chromatic content (apart from an implementation artifact). ChestMNIST is not even plotted. Any color-reliance conclusion must exclude or separately explain all grayscale datasets, not only an absent one.

predicted_errors.error_location: Section 5.2, Remote Sensing paragraph versus Figure 4g–i
predicted_errors.supporting_evidence: The Remote Sensing text says Figure 4g–i reports UCMerced, RSD46-WHU, DeepGlobe, PatternNet, and AID. The figure labels instead list AID, EuroSAT, NWPU, RESISC45, and UC Merced. Only AID and UC Merced overlap. Therefore the reported RS trends cannot be attributed to a definite set of datasets, and the associated citations and domain-average interpretation are ambiguous.

The cross-domain comparison is presented as evidence of domain-specific reliance, but Figure 4 compares models trained under different initialization regimes: CV models are ImageNet-pretrained and fine-tuned, while MI and RS models are trained from scratch. Pretraining is explicitly treated elsewhere in the paper as a factor that changes reliance and robustness. Thus the Figure 4 domain differences are confounded by training initialization, rather than isolating domain characteristics as claimed. A matched from-scratch comparison for all domains, or matched pretrained comparisons where feasible, is required for the stated causal interpretation.
